biography: Born in Christchurch, New Zealand, Marcus Armstrong practically grew up in a kart. His father, a weekend warrior racer himself, instilled a love for speed in Marcus from a young age. He dominated the local karting scene before making the leap to formula cars, where he faced initial struggles adapting to the downforce and braking techniques. A pivotal moment came during a wet race at Manfeild, where his raw talent shone through, allowing him to make a series of daring overtakes and secure a podium finish. This result caught the attention of a prominent racing academy, launching his international career. After years of racing overseas, Marcus made a return to F-USA in 2023, seeking a new challenge and a chance to compete closer to home.
drivingStyle: Armstrong is known for his incredibly smooth and precise driving style. He prioritizes tire management above all else, often sacrificing early pace to ensure he has the grip needed for a late-race charge. He is unflappable under pressure, rarely making mistakes even when battling wheel-to-wheel. His corner entry is calculated and efficient, minimizing wheel slip and maximizing momentum. He's not the most aggressive driver, but his consistency and strategic approach often pay dividends.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their Formula Ford days. Their aggressive on-track battles often resulted in collisions and heated exchanges.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about control, patience, and knowing when to strike."
careerHighlight: Winning the F-USA race at Watkins Glen in 2023. He started from the back of the grid due to a mechanical issue and drove a masterful race, overtaking several cars in the final laps to secure the victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of a Formula 3 race at Spa-Francorchamps in 2014. The incident cost him valuable championship points and shook his confidence for a brief period.
